facts.raw_span: a 2-month history of a painless mass on the right side of the frontal bone
the mass measured approximately 4.0 × 3.5 cm
was well circumscribed, soft, nonmobile, and non-tender
Laboratory studies and neurologic examination were unremarkable
a large, circumscribed radiolucent lesion in the right frontal bone without adjacent soft-tissue swelling
a lytic lesion of the frontal bone with a soap-bubble appearance, cortical destruction of the inner and outer tables, and an associated soft-tissue component
a lobulated frontal-bone mass measuring 3.7 × 3.3 × 2.8 cm
was hypointense on T1-weighted images, hyperintense on T2-weighted images, and showed avid enhancement on postcontrast sequences

concepts.why: The presence of a circumscribed radiolucent lesion in the right frontal bone with a soap-bubble appearance and cortical destruction is consistent with an osteoma.
The soap-bubble appearance and avid enhancement on postcontrast sequences are characteristic of a hemangioma of bone.
The lytic lesion with a soap-bubble appearance and cortical destruction, along with the presence of a soft-tissue component, is consistent with a giant cell tumor.
The soap-bubble appearance and fluid-fluid levels, along with the presence of a soft-tissue component, are characteristic of an aneurysmal bone cyst.
The presence of a lytic lesion with a soap-bubble appearance and cortical destruction, along with the possibility of hyperparathyroidism, is consistent with a brown tumor.

rationales.F01: Painless mass is less typical of osteoma and more typical of other bone lesions
rationales.F03: Well-circumscribed, soft, nonmobile, and non-tender mass is more typical of benign bone lesions
rationales.F04: Unremarkable laboratory studies and neurologic examination make brown tumor of hyperparathyroidism less likely
rationales.F06: Lytic lesion with soap-bubble appearance and cortical destruction is highly suggestive of giant cell tumor or aneurysmal bone cyst
rationales.F08: Hypointense on T1-weighted images, hyperintense on T2-weighted images, and avid enhancement on postcontrast sequences is highly suggestive of giant cell tumor or aneurysmal bone cyst

frontier_selector.rationale: The soap-bubble appearance and cortical destruction of the inner and outer tables are characteristic of a giant cell tumor, and the patient's presentation with a painless mass is also consistent with this diagnosis.
